When most of the pumping energy is derived from nuclear generating plants, a large pumped storage plant will produce a large reduction in the production cost of electric energy and result in a large reduction in the amount of costly fossil fuel consumption.
The environmental impacts of the pumped storage project when considered apart from the sources of pumping energy are similar to those of the conventional hydroelectric project, except for larger fluctuations of reservoir water levels in the former. When considered along with the sources of pumping energy, the environmental impacts will depend upon the type of plants which supply most of the pumping energy.
8.2.3 Simple-Cycle Combustion Turbines
The beneficial aspects of a simple-cycle combustion turbine alternative are: (1) relatively small physical size per kilowatt of capacity, permitting installation at existing plants, (2) no cooling water required which adds to the flexibility in siting, (3) a short letime for plant construction, (4) low capital cost, and (5) relatively short time required from a cold start to full load.
The negative aspects of the combustion turbine are: (1) its low efficiency, which results in high fuel costs per megawatt-hour production and consumption of liquid and gaseous-type fossil fuels which are in critical supply; (2) operating and maintenance costs are historically high, particularly when operating for long periods of time; (3) the starting characteristics of the combustion turbine make it unreliable and, depending on the system characteristics, it could not be considered part of the ready or spinning reserve capacity; (4) at light loads it is too inefficient to be kept on-the-line; and (5) when water injection is required to reduce NOX emission, a supply of high quality injection water must be available.
Negative environmental impacts include: (1) release of combustion by-products into the atmosphere, and (2) siting problems associated with State and local zoning ordinances. Use of synthetic fuels obtained from the gasification or liquefaction of coal could provide a low-sulphur source of fuel.
